name: Mutualism
summary: Mutualism is the libertarian socialist market economy associated with Pierre-Joseph Proudhon. It holds that labour is the basis of property and value, treats rent, profit and non-nominal interest as exploitation, and would end them through free mutual credit and exchange at cost among artisans, peasants and worker-run associations. Government is to be dissolved into contracts between free groups in a decentralised federation.
scope: The economic and political theory of Proudhon (What Is Property?, General Idea of the Revolution, the Bank of the People) and the mutualists who followed him, including Josiah Warren and Benjamin Tucker's four monopolies. It does not cover the biological sense of mutualism, anarcho-communism or later left-libertarian revivals, and Proudhon's patriarchal and bigoted private views are noted but not treated as defining the doctrine.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Mutualists would meet health needs through mutual-aid associations and cooperatives, not a tax-funded state service; inferred from their rejection of the state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A statutory wage floor accepts wage labour and state regulation, both of which mutualists want to dissolve through cooperative ownership; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mutualism is a market system of artisans, sole proprietors and cooperatives, so it prefers exchange to state allocation, though not capitalist markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Proudhon wanted 'no State, not even for a servant', and mutualists put industry under workers' associations rather than nationalising it.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proudhon aimed at equal fortunes through reciprocity and free credit and hoped to abolish taxation, so redistribution by taxing is not his method; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Proudhon backed workers' associations and councils as protest against the wage system; strikes themselves go unaddressed in the sources, so the answer is inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Proudhon declared property theft and mutualists make land titles conditional on occupancy and use, though they defend possession of one's own product.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mutualists want to remove state-backed monopolies and replace corporations with associations, not to add state regulators; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Mutualists reject state welfare as a palliative but do not argue from dependency; they would replace it with mutual aid and an end to exploitation. Inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Proudhon wanted large-scale workplaces run by workers' associations with an undivided share held by each member, and mutualism is defined by workers' control of production.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from Proudhon's hostility to the state and its police power; mutualists would not trade liberty for state security.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the anti-authority stance that adults' choices are not for the state to police.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from rejection of state coercion, though Proudhon personally held bigoted views.

strong-leader.rationale: Proudhon rejected dictatorship and centralised rule as tyranny and wanted no government, not even a direct one.

state-harmful.rationale: Proudhon writes 'I want no State, not even for a servant' and sees the state dissolving into economic contracts.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his wish to replace standing armies with armed workers' associations and from distrust of state restriction.

empower-police-military.rationale: Proudhon put police under local control, wanted standing armies replaced and 'collective force' to supersede public force.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Adherents split: Proudhon was a strict moralist on sex, while modern mutualists are libertarian about consensual adult exchange.

decide-locally.rationale: Proudhon's universal federalism rests on sovereign communes, districts and provinces joined by contract, and he saw centralisation as a return to feudalism.

rehabilitation.rationale: Proudhon opposed the state's sword of punishment, so reform over retribution is the nearer fit; the sources say little on prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Proudhon was a committed defender of marriage and patriarchal family order, though modern mutualists may differ.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic: Proudhon's own sexual morality was conservative, while modern mutualists favour freedom of association; adherents split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Proudhon's patriarchal moralism and modern libertarian mutualism point opposite ways.

more-religion-public.rationale: Proudhon wanted free worship paid for by participants and saw church-state ties as shoring up authority, and he linked Church, state and capital.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; a state programme conflicts with mutualist anti-statism while the aim of ending coercive privilege fits it.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Proudhon treated sex roles as grounded in nature and male strength, so he would reject the constructivist claim.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Proudhon denied political nationality and thought nations were just birthplaces; local mores matter more to him than a national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: He wanted a peaceful but thorough social liquidation that replaces existing institutions, so he would not defer to established ones.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mutualists oppose border-enforcing states and political nationality; inferred, though Proudhon's private xenophobia is documented.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: His federalism is of free communes by contract, not a world authority above them; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Split: Proudhon defended protection of weaker producers early on while Tucker's tradition counts tariffs as a monopoly to abolish.

nation-first.rationale: Proudhon argued that nationalism blocks economic solidarity and that governments perpetuate conflict.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from his view that states make war and that force exercised by governments is illegitimate.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of political nationality and federal unity across borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; mutualism is concerned with who owns capital, not with the scale of growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no mutualist position on climate, and state mandates conflict with its anti-statism while collective action fits it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Proudhon valued industrial progress and collective force, but he made justice and institutional reform, not technology, the solution.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic: nothing in Proudhon or later mutualists bears on energy sources, and neither a state nuclear programme nor cooperative energy follows clearly from their principles.

revolution-justified.rationale: Proudhon's whole project is a social revolution, which he held should spread by example rather than arms.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from rejection of governmental hierarchy and of party leaders' formulas, but he did not address expertise as such.

central-planning.rationale: Proudhon condemns centralisation as a hierarchy of functionaries and says true centralisation is equality of wealth.

socialized-markets.rationale: Mutualism is the classic worker-cooperative market economy, though it does not favour public ownership of firms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Mutualists would make land use-tenure conditional and abolish land tax and rent rather than rely on state taxation of land value.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Proudhon backed inheritance of personal possessions but not of instruments of labour, yet would not use the state to tax it; adherents split.

basic-income.rationale: State-funded universal payment conflicts with anti-statism and cost-based exchange; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tucker's mutualists counted tariffs among the four monopolies, though Proudhon himself had protectionist leanings.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Proudhon rejected a central bank under a finance minister in favour of many local lenders and mutual credit.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mutualism aims at an economy without concentrated capital or land, with equal fortunes held as artisans' and peasants' possessions and associated enterprises.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Proudhon opposed the wage system but retained money and exchange at cost; the label labour notes is disputed, so the combined claim is rejected.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Proudhon opposed a central bank, and mutualists would replace it with competing mutual banks issuing credit at cost.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting prices are the opposite of contract between free equals and local credit.

one-party-rule.rationale: Proudhon opposed dictatorship and Jacobin democracy and wanted society without authority.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He treated God and King as the foundation of conservatism and expected monarchs to leave the stage.

democracy-best.rationale: Proudhon rejects government of any kind, even direct government, and sharply criticised Jacobin democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Proudhon calls direct legislation a false application of the principle of authority and rejects even direct government.

workers-councils.rationale: Proudhon wanted industrial organisation to replace political power and supported workers' associations and councils, though not as a state.

right-to-secede.rationale: Proudhon's federalism is of contractual groups that can secede, though sources do not state it for regions as such.

natural-rulers.rationale: Government of man by man is oppression, so no natural class of rulers is admitted.

political-violence-never.rationale: Proudhon saw revolution as a moral transformation and criticised the violence of June 1848, but accepted force from necessity.

war-builds-character.rationale: Proudhon held that governments keep nations at war and that war loses its purpose; his own War and Peace is ambivalent.

separate-church-state.rationale: He wants worship funded only by its adherents and the state cut loose from religion.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Contract replaces law in his scheme, and he rejects church-state ties as supports of authority.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Proudhon replaces public force with collective force and voluntary contracts; Tucker-style mutualists accept defence associations. Inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Proudhon held nations are not political bodies and expected economic solidarity to end war.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Proudhon opposed nationalism and said mutualism leaves no political nationality or fatherland.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He rejected class war and Marxist history in favour of reciprocity and cooperation, though he saw exploitation.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Equality of conditions is for Proudhon the true principle of right, and he sought equal fortunes, but he rejects distribution by need.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from the use-and-occupancy rule for land and from local autonomy.

colonial-reparations.rationale: State-to-state transfers would not suit a stateless federalism; inferred and anachronistic.

civilizational-union.rationale: Proudhon wanted communal federation by contract, not unions defined by civilisation; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mutualism rests on reciprocity and mutual guarantee of exchange at cost rather than praise of self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Proudhon stressed individual sovereignty and freely accepted contract, not subordinating individual rights to community duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources do not discuss the value of nature; mutualist texts concern property, credit and the state, so neither answer can be inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed positively; Proudhon opposed Malthusian causes of poverty but not directly measures.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Proudhon welcomed industry and collective force as sources of wealth and wanted them organised by workers.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; Proudhon prized industry but sought institutional change first.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the mutualist emphasis on individual liberty and from the absence of any authority entitled to forbid personal choices.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from rejection of any governing apparatus replacing self-government and contract.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from hostility to state surveillance.

restore-past-order.rationale: Proudhon denounced conservatism as preserving authority and aimed at revolution.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Proudhon distrusted formulas but argued from principles of justice; adherents split.

direct-action.rationale: Mutualists build banks and cooperatives directly in place of the state and parliament, but Proudhon also stood for election in 1848.

means-match-ends.rationale: Proudhon held revolution should spread by example and contract, not by arms or authority.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Proudhon valued industry, division of labour and collective force as productive.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Proudhon lists division of labour among real economic forces and keeps it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Proudhon explicitly rejects 'to each according to his needs' because someone must judge need, and bases exchange on cost and liberty.

production-for-use.rationale: Mutualists treat profit as exploitation and want exchange at cost, though through markets.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Mutualists treat profit, rent and non-nominal interest as forms of exploitation of labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Proudhon opposed dictatorship and Louis Blanc's state socialism, and criticised centralised rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Proudhon held peasants could not practically be organised in associations, and independent peasants and artisans are sovereign in their work.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Proudhon blamed governments for war, with capitalism joined to church and state; adherents differ.

taxation-theft.rationale: Proudhon wanted taxation abolished through mutual credit, though the sources do not say 'theft'.

harm-principle.rationale: Inferred from the contract-based and liberty-focused view that coercion is restricted.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Proudhon gave real standing to collective force and federated groups while stressing individual sovereignty; adherents split.

conscription.rationale: Proudhon in 1848 proposed brief compulsory service for citizens, but mutualists as anti-militarists reject conscription generally.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Proudhon prefers contract and the right of groups to leave over majority voting.

state-as-business.rationale: Proudhon wanted the state abolished, not run on commercial lines.

positive-liberty.rationale: Mutualists hold that monopolies of credit and land deny workers the means to act; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Mutualist texts do not weigh the political power of the press or universities against elected officials, and Proudhon distrusted all parties of rulers alike.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racism was private for Proudhon and not part of his political system; mainstream mutualism rejects it.

organic-representation.rationale: Proudhon's federation links communes and trade bodies through contract, though without a corporatist state.

total-state.rationale: Proudhon's demand for 'no State, not even for a servant' and his attack on centralisation as a hierarchy of functionaries are the opposite of a state directing all of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Proudhon opposed nationalism, and mutualism has no national palingenesis.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Proudhon held war purposeless once economic solidarity replaces political rule.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Contract between free equals is the only moral bond he accepts.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom-style obligations to a lord contradict the mutualist ideas of free contract between equals and of land held by those who work it.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Proudhon treated justice as discoverable by reason yet also denounced how law and economics serve privilege, so adherents could answer either way.

universal-morality.rationale: Proudhon grounded justice in reason and equality; moderately confident only by inference.

single-common-good.rationale: Proudhon accepts contractual reciprocity among free groups, not one common good fixed by authority.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Anachronistic; Proudhon denied political nationhood, and his own antisemitism is documented but not a programme.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship by return to a homeland assumes political nationality, which Proudhon denied; inferred from that, with no direct statement.

revive-national-language.rationale: Making a revived language the state language is a nationalist project; inferred from Proudhon's view that nations are birthplaces, not political bodies.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Proudhon wanted workers' associations with elected managers, though not a public vote.

school-vouchers.rationale: State funding mechanisms conflict with his anti-statism; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Proudhon wanted ample credit but opposed state-run finance; adherents split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Proudhon wanted politics dissolved into economic organisation under contract.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rejects rulers entirely, though he stresses moral example in spreading revolution.

national-self-determination.rationale: He denied political nationality and wanted communal federation, not nation-states.

force-without-un.rationale: Proudhon held that governments perpetuate war and that economic solidarity would remove its purpose, so a state choosing to use force abroad finds no support.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Proudhon opposed religion and grounded justice in reason, but also valued sentiments; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not applicable to a stateless theory; adherents would not frame welfare by citizenship.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists reject state welfare but prize labour.

class-collaboration.rationale: Proudhon opposed class war yet wanted to end the employer-employee relation itself.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Proudhon was a revolutionary but not a destroyer of culture.

dominated-front.rationale: A bloc defined by national grievance runs against his dislike of nationalism and of power politics between states; inferred and anachronistic.

workers-nation.rationale: Proudhon argued that nationalism blocks economic unity and said mutualism leaves no political nationality, so organising workers along national lines is contrary to it.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Proudhon held patriarchal views, but he rejected law in principle; modern mutualists split.

ban-interest.rationale: Proudhon opposed interest but preferred it remain voluntary and fade through mutual credit, not be banned.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: State classification by race conflicts with equal contract and the abolition of state coercion.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Proudhon linked capital, government and the Church in a trinity of absolutism and said the state upholds property.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic: mutualism has no stated view on energy production, and the question turns on state policy that it does not address.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from a federal, contractual view without political nationality.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy of this sort has no place in mutualist theory, and Proudhon's private bigotry was not part of it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Proudhon rejected representation by parties, but PR as a lesser reform is not addressed.

national-mission.rationale: Proudhon opposed spreading institutions by arms and nationalism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Proudhon defended male dominance as natural rather than analysing it as structural.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He held politics takes precedence over justice and denounced party leaders' schemes.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State eugenics is coercion against persons, contradicting the contractual, anti-authority basis of mutualism; inferred from that.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state force and for local control of police.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Proudhon wants no State at all, so even a minimal state is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not part of his political system, and contrary to equal contract.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality is Proudhon's central principle of right, although his private prejudices contradicted it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Mutualist federation does not depend on a simultaneous revolution; inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not discussed; mutualist land theory (title by occupancy and use) cuts both ways on settler land and adherents split.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Proudhon's federation of contractual groups prefers legal plurality.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Proudhon wanted worship to be free and funded by those who take part, with the state out of religion, so legal limits on conversion are rejected.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; a state ban on a practice conflicts with the mutualist preference for voluntary arrangements, so mildly negative by inference.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: He wanted religion funded only by its participants and away from the state.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Proudhon wanted the state dissolved, not strengthened by circumstance.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Contract is for Proudhon the only moral bond free beings accept, and mutualists say people are bound only by obligations freely accepted.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mutualist exchange is reciprocal at cost; mercantilist aims are foreign to it.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal is coercion that contradicts contract and federation.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Inferred from contract and anti-coercion, but Proudhon admitted a right of force from necessity.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Proudhon lists competition among forces but speaks of reciprocity and expects war to end.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Proudhon opposed state suppression and held that authority rests on contract, so outlawing parties is disfavoured; inferred rather than stated.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: His rejection of authority and government as oppression fits the republican idea of freedom as non-domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Federation checks power but Proudhon wanted to dissolve government, so partial.

vanguard-party.rationale: Proudhon rejected party formulas and dictatorship; revolution is made by criticism and example.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Equality of conditions favours the poor; no express priority principle.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Proudhon wanted rent abolished and occupiers to hold their homes, so tenants gaining ownership fits, though through reciprocity rather than a state scheme.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism and support for workers' associations.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Proudhon located the cause of lasting poverty in property, rent and interest that take the worker's product, not in numbers of people.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: His federalism joins diverse groups by contract and is hostile to national homogeneity; no source states it on this precise claim.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Proudhon wanted government dissolved and elected managers in workplaces; sortition for public office is not discussed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Mutualists oppose arbitrary state power and hold that authority rests only on contract, so emergency suspension of legal protections is rejected.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Mutualists seek cost price through competition, not state price fixing; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Control of information by a party-state is the kind of authority Proudhon wanted abolished; inferred from his anti-state stance.

party-commands-army.rationale: Proudhon wanted standing armies replaced and no ruling party commanding force; party control of arms is the reverse.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Waiting periods presuppose a political nationality that Proudhon denied; inferred and not discussed by the sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Proudhon proposed ending pensions for state functionaries and having localities pay their employees.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Mutualists hold majority decisions do not bind dissenting minorities.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Proudhon's federalism envisaged contractual federation across borders, but not an EU as such.

head-commands-forces.rationale: A single head holding command of forces and ministers is the centralised authority that Proudhon identified with tyranny and a return to feudalism.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Proudhon opposed hierarchy and church-state ties and wanted free worship, so episcopal government is not something he would favour; no direct statement.

clerical-rule.rationale: Proudhon placed the Church with capital and the state in a trinity of absolutism, so rule by senior clergy is firmly rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Proudhon blamed governments for war and wanted peoples united by economic solidarity.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: State censorship is coercion that mutualism opposes, though Proudhon was himself a moralist about art; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Mutualists wish to dissolve government rather than manage its offices, but dislike entrenched power; the question is not addressed directly.

recall-officials.rationale: Contractual accountability of delegates fits his view, though he rejected representation.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Proudhon opposed militarism and expected war to lose its purpose, so ending permanent military alliances fits; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Proudhon wanted rent abolished and occupiers to own their homes.

people-in-arms.rationale: He wanted workers' collective force in place of standing armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Proudhon valued independent peasants but also industry and workers' associations, and no source says rural life is morally better.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification as a national goal assumes political nationality, which Proudhon rejected; inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources say nothing about university graduates, and mutualism is about economic organisation rather than class cultural resentments.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from federalism, but he held some prejudiced views.

death-penalty.rationale: Proudhon criticised the state's sword of punishment and its resort to coercion, so he leans against execution; he is not documented on this directly.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Proudhon's conservative sexual morality and mutualist distrust of state schooling point against, while modern mutualists favour equality of the sexes; adherents split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Proudhon wanted the state separated from religion and blamed church-state ties for supporting authority, so state schools teaching creationism is rejected.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Proudhon held strict views on sex and morals, yet the mutualist hostility to state coercion argues the other way; adherents split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based citizenship builds in a political nationality, which Proudhon denied; inferred and not discussed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from his federalism of self-governing communes and provinces, which leaves cultural matters to local groups.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; mutualism wants free worship and no general law, but the question presumes state law that mutualists would not defend.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Proudhon's mores were conservative; mutualists liberty-minded.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Mutualists treat non-nominal interest as exploitation, so cancelling interest-bearing debts of poor countries fits their view; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Proudhon held political change meaningless without economic organisation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Proudhon doubted representative assemblies and wanted contract to replace law, so an elected assembly to write a constitution is not his route.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Proudhon placed liberty and contract at the centre, and mutualists reject coercion by rulers for any purpose.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: State-run aid sits poorly with exchange at cost and mutual credit; Proudhon is not documented on international aid, so this is inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Mutualists wanted standing armies replaced and war ended, so national nuclear weapons are contrary to their view; anachronistic.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Proudhon rejected government even in direct form, so a directly elected head of state is not what he wants.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Proudhon opposed a central bank and favoured local mutual credit.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Treating historic homeland as non-negotiable assumes nationalism, which Proudhon opposed; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Legitimate property for mutualists is bounded by labour and use.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Mutualists reject the state-socialist path and call it state capitalism; anachronistic.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic, with no mutualist position; state precaution conflicts with anti-statism while collective risk management is accepted.

collective-defense.rationale: Permanent alliances bind states in war, which Proudhon wanted to end, though mutualists accept collective defence by voluntary groups; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He wanted church and state separated, not state control of religion.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Proudhon wanted no head of state at all, so a symbolic one is a lesser matter but not endorsed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Mutualist federalism is built from contracting groups that can leave, so force to keep a region in a state is rejected.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A region joining a larger state while keeping its own economic and legal order resembles Proudhon's federation by contract, though he wanted no state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Proudhon named God and King as the foundation of conservatism and expected monarchs to leave the stage.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Proudhon wanted taxation reduced and eventually unnecessary; how rates are structured is not discussed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Proudhon blamed property and institutions for despotism and poverty.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Proudhon saw contract between free equals as the only moral bond, which rules out a ruler exempt from law.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic, and unrelated to mutualist concerns.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Proudhon wanted the political system dissolved into economic contract rather than a balanced constitution of the few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Mass praise of a ruler as the embodiment of the nation contradicts Proudhon's dislike of authority and his criticism of Napoleonic and Robespierrist rule.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; Proudhon's patriarchal family views and modern mutualist liberalism diverge.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Proudhon rejected state socialism and relied on reciprocity rather than class war, and mutualists see no ruling party to restore capitalism; inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Mutualists make land titles conditional on occupancy and use and oppose rent, which supports giving land to its cultivators, though not by state seizure.

refugee-return.rationale: Return to homes fits the occupancy-and-use basis for land and contract between persons; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Proudhon denied political nationality and thought nations were birthplaces, so claims to territory because co-nationals live there are rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Free worship and separation of religion from the state are part of Proudhon's scheme, so legal punishment for leaving a religion is rejected.

women-must-cover.rationale: State compulsion over dress is coercion against persons, contrary to contract and liberty, though Proudhon's own views on women were conservative.

common-currency.rationale: Mutualists favour mutual credit and competing local banks over a single currency managed centrally; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Union by ancestry is a nationalist project; Proudhon wanted federation by contract among communes, not by kinship.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Self-governing cultural groups within a state resemble Proudhon's federation of autonomous groups, though he wanted no state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from federal contract and denial of political nationality, which favour equal rights in place of emigration to a national state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Proudhon put economic forces first, though with justice immanent.

ban-cartels.rationale: Mutualists oppose monopoly but through competing cooperatives rather than state prohibition.

no-bailouts.rationale: Mutualists oppose state-protected privilege and banking monopoly, so public money for failing banks or firms conflicts with their view; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Mutualists hold that majority decisions do not bind dissenting minorities and distrust unrestrained majorities, so courts limiting a majority are not objectionable.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism and Proudhon's patriarchal views; no mutualist source speaks to quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Proudhon based economic life on reciprocal exchange among producers and wanted nations to lose their political barriers, so autarkic blocs run against it.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards imposed by treaties among states are not a mutualist method; inferred and anachronistic.

moral-incentives.rationale: Proudhon rejected 'to each according to needs' and wanted exchange on cost and liberty, not a sense of social duty replacing material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Proudhon held that revolution spreads by example and criticism and not by arms, and criticised the violence of the June days.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Proudhon wanted equal fortunes and inheritance restricted for instruments of labour.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Teaching history around one's nation or civilisation is nationalist education that Proudhon would oppose; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Proudhon described the government of man by man as oppression, which includes one society ruling another.

patriotic-education.rationale: Proudhon opposed nationalism and said mutualism leaves no political nationality or fatherland, so teaching national pride is rejected.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Mutualists oppose state-granted privilege of any kind, which favours ending preferences, though they also oppose racial discrimination; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Proudhon's Bank of the People was a mutual bank of its subscribers, and he opposed a central bank under a finance minister.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Proudhon saw interest and rent as drawing wealth from workers, leading to crisis, but he made no claim about collapse; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Mutualist federalism and opposition to expansion run against a country seeking influence over former imperial lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Mutualists favour exchange at cost among producers and Tucker's school favoured free trade; breaking economic ties is not their remedy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Proudhon located exploitation in interest, rent and profit within each economy, not in a split between national workforces; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Mutualists value freedom of association yet reject exploitation and bigotry; adherents split and sources do not decide.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Mutualists want authority bound by contract rather than a state constitution, so entrenched state-enforced rights are not a mutualist device.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed by mutualist sources; contract theory could treat unconsulted treaties as void, but no source applies it.

elective-rulers.rationale: Proudhon called himself a democrat and republican in the 1860s and opposed hereditary rule, though he wanted no rulers at all.

minority-veto.rationale: Robert Graham reads Proudhon as holding that people are bound only by obligations they freely accept, so majority decisions do not bind a dissenting minority.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Proudhon criticised rulers who break contract and held authority rests on consent, so resisting a lawless ruler fits; no source states it directly.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Proudhon wanted political power dissolved into economic contract and doubted parliaments, so parliamentary supremacy is not endorsed.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Mutualist texts do not address animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Mutualist texts do not address animals, so neither answer can be inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Mutualists seek reciprocity and an end to exploitation, not charity from the wealthy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Proudhon was a deputy, journalist and organiser, and wanted social revolution, though he later preferred economic action to electoral politics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Mutualist sources do not discuss mass culture or hegemony.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Proudhon linked state, capital and church but did not theorise consent through culture; adherents are not recorded on this.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Mutualist sources discuss exploitation within exchange, not a world system extracting surplus from poor countries.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving public offices for the native-born assumes political nationality, which Proudhon rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: Proudhon opposed direction from a centre and favoured federal autonomy, which favours each party choosing its own road; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Mutualist sources do not address foreign aid or development finance, though they favour local credit and self-help.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Demanding territory lost in war is a nationalist aim, and Proudhon opposed nationalism and expected war to lose its purpose.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Mutualists oppose rule by any group over another and favour equal federation, which tells against hereditary political leadership; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; mutualist sources do not address constitutional values.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; mutualists oppose both authoritarian right and state communism, but the question of equivalence is not addressed.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic: mutualist sources do not address the American Civil War, and modern mutualists in the Warren and Tucker tradition treat slavery as the cause; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Mutualist sources do not address monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Mutualist sources do not address male disadvantage, and Proudhon's views on sex roles do not map on to it.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Mutualist sources do not address domestic violence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Proudhon wanted federalism and contract everywhere, yet not Western parliaments; the claim is not directly addressed.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Proudhon wanted standing armies replaced and no rulers, so a political guardian role for armed forces is firmly rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: Proudhon held domestic work belongs to the family and wife's place; modern mutualists may differ; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Proudhon championed family and its duties as a basis of morality; inferred from his defence of the patriarchal family.

office-by-exam.rationale: Mutualist sources do not address civil service recruitment, though Proudhon wanted functionaries paid locally.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Blocking takeovers is state economic control, which mutualists would not use; they would end monopoly through competing cooperatives.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Proudhon opposed divorce and held marriage indissoluble, but mutualist liberalism since may differ; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Proudhon rejected representation but his contractual view implies delegates answerable to those who bind them; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Mutualists favour mutual associations over both state and private companies, and the sources do not address pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Mutualists hold land titles should depend on occupancy and use, though they place ownership in the user or association, not in the nation or community.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Proudhon wanted taxation abolished through mutual credit, so parliamentary budget control is not a mutualist concern; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Compelling one language fits a centralising state, while Proudhon's federation lets communes govern themselves; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Restrictions by nationality contradict use-and-occupancy tenure, which does not depend on nationality; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Treating unequal outcomes as discrimination implies state enforcement mutualists dislike, though they oppose bigotry; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Mutualist sources do not address consumption; Proudhon prized modest property of one's own.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Governments arming foreign insurgents is state war-making that Proudhon blamed for keeping nations in conflict.

corporate-influence.rationale: Mutualists hold that state-backed monopolies of credit, land and capital serve the wealthy, which fits complaints about corporate influence over government.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: State restriction of funding conflicts with anti-statism and contract, though it is not addressed; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: State family incentives conflict with anti-statism, though Proudhon valued family; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Occupancy-and-use tenure favours residents holding land, but restricting sales is a state or local rule mutualists do not address.

job-guarantee.rationale: Proudhon wanted workers to own and control their enterprises through associations and credit, not rely on state employment; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Mutualist sources do not address democratic peace, though Proudhon thought economic solidarity, not regime type, ends war.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Proudhon held that contract is the only moral bond free and equal beings can accept, so there is no general duty to obey law as such.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from Proudhon's opposition to governments' wars and his federal view of free peoples.

industrial-unions.rationale: Proudhon backed workers' associations in industries needing combined labour, so organising across an industry fits; he did not discuss union forms.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Proudhon's private diaries were hostile to Jews, but such claims form no part of mutualist theory and its scholars reject them as political thought.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Proudhon defended marriage and the family as institutions to be kept, though he wanted no state, and mutualists since may differ.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state secrecy and the contract basis of authority.

local-production.rationale: Proudhon's agro-industrial federation and producer-consumer reciprocity at cost favour exchange close to home; not stated directly.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Mutualism denies national sovereignty as such, so privileging one state's courts over international bodies is not its aim; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Mutualists organise banks, associations and federations, which are formal, but also act through voluntary groups; the sources do not decide.

religious-nation.rationale: Proudhon opposed church-state ties and denied political nationality, so defining a nation by religion is rejected.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Ritual submission of states to a great power is the hierarchy of authority Proudhon rejected in favour of equal federation.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Proudhon's decentralisation and local control of resources favour regions keeping revenue; not stated directly.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Mutualists keep personal property in one's labour product, but favour possession and associations rather than common ownership of production, so adherents split.

defeat-communism.rationale: Proudhon opposed authoritarian communism but wanted reform by example, not defeat of rivals by force; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Mutualists would want services run by cooperatives and mutual societies rather than a tax-funded mix of providers; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Proudhon attacked the Church and predicted Christianity's decline, though he also had a view of justice immanent in humanity; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Proudhon credited collective force and industry with creating wealth while condemning appropriation; adherents split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Proudhon did not hold women's equality as a goal and treated economic change as aimed at workers; modern mutualists may differ.

socialized-care.rationale: Proudhon placed housework and childcare in the family, and mutualists oppose state provision; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: State language policy is a nationalist project that mutualists reject; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Mutualism rests on contract, so agreements between a government and a nation should hold unless both agree to change them; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Proudhon's federation of self-governing communes and associations fits, though mutualists keep individual possession rather than common property.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-encouraged settlement to alter population balance is political nationalism that mutualists reject; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Proudhon opposed both capitalism and state socialism and presented mutualism as a third course, which Wikipedia's biographical entry on him describes.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Claims on historical grounds sit poorly with title based on occupancy and use, which depends on present use; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Mutualist theory has no place for denial of historical atrocities, though Proudhon's own private diaries were hostile to Jews; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Mutualists oppose state coercion over private conduct, though Proudhon was morally conservative; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Proudhon opposed dictatorship, Jacobin democracy and the state's sword of power, so suppressing opposition for order is rejected.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Proudhon wanted free worship and no state support of religion, so punishing blasphemy or false religion is rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Exploitation of one territory for another's benefit is the kind of extraction mutualism condemns as appropriation of labour; inferred from that.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious duty of armed resistance is not a mutualist doctrine, though they accept defensive resistance; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious law as a standard of legitimacy contradicts contract as the basis of authority; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Proudhon wanted workplaces run by workers' associations with elected managers and self-governing communes, though he rejected government by direct legislation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Proudhon located oppression in capital, state and church and did not accept feminist analysis; modern mutualists may differ.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; mutualist sources do not address it and adherents are likely split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Proudhon rejected both capitalism and state socialism and claimed a third course, which favours moving beyond left-right; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Proudhon argued that workers produce collective force and receive only wages, so labour under the wage system is separated from its product.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Mutualism has no such claim; Proudhon opposed nationalism and cultural exclusion in politics, though he held bigoted private views.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Proudhon held that contract is the only moral bond, and linked God and King as conservative foundations of authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Separation of religion and state favours it, while freedom favours the opposite; mutualist sources do not address it.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; mutualists value voluntary contract yet oppose coercion in unequal bargains.

social-market-economy.rationale: Mutualists want markets of workers' associations without capital's returns, not a state-managed mix with social protection; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Proudhon proposed that industrial associations replace standing armies and expected war to lose its purpose.

rich-first.rationale: Proudhon sought equality of fortunes and an end to interest, rent and profit, so letting some grow rich first is contrary.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from Proudhon's opposition to power politics and militarism.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Mutualists hold that authority rests only on the consent of those bound, so annexation without consent is illegitimate; Proudhon is not documented on annexation specifically.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Proudhon opposed governments' wars and held that federal groups are free to leave by contract, so troops sent to stop an ally leaving a bloc are rejected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Free mutual credit through a Bank of Exchange or People's Bank is the central economic proposal of Proudhon and the mutualist tradition.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Proudhon rejected government by hereditary authority and wanted the state dissolved into federated contracts, so inherited office is rejected.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Mutualists oppose interest-bearing finance and exploitation by creditors; inferred that they would resist lenders' conditions, which were never discussed.

property-franchise.rationale: Mutualism treats labour as the basis of property and would not restrict political rights to owners; Proudhon opposed privilege of property.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Proudhon's patriarchal views are noted as outside the doctrine, and nature's domination was not addressed; mutualists are split.

reification.rationale: The theory says rent, profit and interest turn labour into capital's instrument; inferred as close to reification, though Proudhon did not use the concept.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Mutualists hold that capital monopolies make formal rights empty, a point close to the claim; inferred from the four monopolies critique.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Proudhon wanted society to be ruled by contract and by general laws, not arbitrary power; inferred as supportive.

racial-franchise.rationale: The doctrine rests on equal contract among free producers; Proudhon's bigotry is noted but not treated as defining the doctrine.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; Proudhon preferred direct federal contracts to representation, and the sources do not address the internet.

open-government-data.rationale: Proudhon's open federal contracting implies publicity of public dealings; inferred, not directly stated.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Proudhon's anti-clericalism and his preference for free contract suggest rejecting legal marriage restrictions; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Contractual equality is the mutualist rule; Proudhon's private bigotry is noted but is not part of the doctrine.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Proudhon rejected representation but favoured federated assemblies of producers; sources do not address lotteries, so split.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Proudhon was anti-clerical and rejected religion's authority over society; inferred as unconcerned with reforming doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Proudhon holds that rent, profit and interest let owners appropriate others' labour, and mutualism aims to end such accumulation so that producers keep roughly equal means.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Mutualism never addressed the question; inferred from its libertarian, free-association principles, which give no ground to bar people for private conduct.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Mutualism would dissolve government into contracts between free groups, leaving no state to run a public education system that promotes any belief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Proudhon would dissolve government into contract and federation, so policing would be replaced by voluntary arrangements; he does not detail prisons, so this is inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from Proudhon's federalism, in which distinct groups keep their autonomy and deal as equals by contract rather than under a numerical majority.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Mutualists look to mutual aid associations and local cooperatives rather than the state, though they treat this as reciprocity, not charity; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Proudhon distrusts permanent professional rulers and wants public functions revocable and bound by contract, so limits on tenure fit; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Proudhon rejected representative government and parliamentary delegation in favour of direct contracts, so delegating votes sits awkwardly with his view; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The theory predates the issue and is indifferent to it; no position can be inferred from its principles.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Adherents are split: Proudhon held patriarchal private views, while later mutualists such as Tucker supported women's equality.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Adherents are split: Proudhon defended the husband's authority in private writing, while later mutualists favoured equal partnership.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from federation of free groups by contract rather than citizenship in a state.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred: mutualism would end rent through free credit and cost exchange, not by state price caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Tucker's four monopolies include patents and copyright, which mutualists called state-granted monopolies.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Proudhon rejected standing armies, nation and the state, so state-organised youth drilled for national service is contrary to the doctrine.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from opposition to the state, standing armies and war machinery.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from opposition to standing armies and centralised states.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: it dissolves government, so official state recognition is not the mutualist method; atrocities are not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Proudhon and mutualist economics hold labour is the basis of property and treat rent, profit and interest as exploitation.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Proudhon defended war as a social phenomenon in his later work, and mutualists accept defence by free groups; strict pacifism is not their doctrine.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Proudhon criticised nationalism and the nation; continuity from antiquity is not discussed.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: Proudhon held patriarchal views on women and sex, though this is not the doctrine.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: Proudhon's own views were patriarchal; the doctrine itself does not address it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Proudhon rejected the nation, state and religion, so sacralising the national dead conflicts with it.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Proudhon's politics was economic and juridical contract, and he criticised religion.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; mutualism opposes nation-states but not diasporas.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: mutualism focuses on economic reorganisation first, and rejects state-building.

god-not-male.rationale: Proudhon was strongly anti-religious; adherents otherwise have no position.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Proudhon rejected religious authority, but this is a feminist standard not discussed.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: It holds equal free exchange among all, and rejects nation and state favouritism.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: borders by contract between free groups rather than state-imposed merging.

independent-unions.rationale: Mutualists wanted workers to organise freely and federate by contract, independent of any government, which Proudhon's rejection of the state implies.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Proudhon rejected both capitalism and state socialism, so only worker-run associations and mutual credit count as emancipation, not state ownership.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Mutualists would have services run by contract among free associations, not owned by a public authority; inferred from their rejection of the state.

second-chamber.rationale: Proudhon rejected centralised government and replaced it with federation by contract; an additional chamber of government is inferred as foreign to it.

municipal-property.rationale: Mutualism favours property held by occupancy and use, with workers' associations and communes owning together, rather than private capitalists or the state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Proudhon's federalism has communes and groups federate by contract, with the federal body holding only delegated, limited powers.

family-wage.rationale: Proudhon rejected distribution by need and held that pay follows labour; his patriarchal views fit a family wage but his theory ties pay to work.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; no stated position, and mutualists would ask who funds it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Mutualist exchange rests on free credit among users and contract outside state control; the state tracing and blocking payments is inferred as opposed.

online-anonymity.rationale: Mutualists oppose state control of association and exchange; anonymity online is inferred from this, not stated.

person-over-state.rationale: Proudhon held that the state exists only by contract of free individuals and groups and rejected authority over them.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Proudhon wrote on justice and religion, but mutualism does not make a spiritual claim that politics should serve; split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Mutualists hold that groups federate by free contract and no higher authority may override their liberty, so revocable powers contradict it.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; mutualists favoured peasant and small producer farming, but no stated position.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; Proudhon held that cities should federate with the countryside, but no stated line.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Proudhon opposed nationalism and group-identity politics, and mutualism organises by labour and contract, not by race.

racial-pride.rationale: Proudhon opposed nationalism and treated the nation as an artificial state unit, so racial pride fits poorly; his personal bigotry is not part of the doctrine.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Proudhon opposed war and standing armies and favoured federation, with defence by citizens, so force is for defence only.

missingStatements.text: Credit should be issued at cost, without interest, by mutual banks owned by their users.
missingStatements.rationale: Free mutual credit through a Bank of Exchange or People's Bank is the central economic proposal of Proudhon and the mutualist tradition.

missingStatements.text: No seller should charge more than the labour cost of producing or acquiring what is sold.
missingStatements.rationale: Josiah Warren's 'cost the limit of price' and the labour theory of value state exchange at cost as the mutualist rule.

notes: Proudhon's sources contain patriarchal and antisemitic private views that scholars treat as separate from his political programme; modern mutualists (Carson and others) generally reject them, so answers on gender and family are low confidence or split. Whether Proudhon proposed labour currency is disputed. Many answers are inferences from his anti-statism, marked low.
